2506.13051.title: Stress-Testing Multimodal Foundation Models for Crystallographic Reasoning
2506.13051.verdict: CLOSEST NEIGHBOUR, NOT FLAGGED BY THE PLAN. Has a Compositional-Exclusion benchmark, nine VLMs on crystal images, space-group validity scoring. BENCHMARK-DESIGN CLAIM DEMOTED. Ours retains deterministic spglib ground truth with tolerance quarantine and the exact-label 3-level hierarchy.

2605.29446.title: CrystalXRD-Bench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for XRD Peak Indexing Across Diverse Crystalline Materials
2605.29446.verdict: OCCUPIED FOR THE HEADLINE. Published crystallography VLM benchmark reporting failure on rendered images AND separating extraction from reasoning by supplying the CIF. Our difference: a geometric oracle on the images rather than handing over ground-truth text.

2510.16926.title: Res-Bench: Benchmarking the Robustness of Multimodal Large Language Models to Dynamic Resolution Input
2510.16926.verdict: ROW A OCCUPIED as a general question — 14,400 samples over 12 resolution levels with stability metrics. Our resolution finding is a domain instance and a CONFOUND CONTROL, not a contribution.

2506.12776.title: Native Visual Understanding: Resolving Resolution Dilemmas in Vision-Language Models
2506.12776.verdict: ROW A supporting — frames the same 'Resolution Dilemma' and notes benchmarks neglect resolution

2003.14328.title: CRYSPNet: Crystal Structure Predictions via Neural Network
2003.14328.verdict: ROW B NOT OCCUPIED — verdict REVERSED. CRYSPNet predicts symmetry 'based ONLY on its chemical composition', the OPPOSITE input to our cell-metric control. Different and harder task. Cited instead as the reason our COMPOSITION-EXCLUSION split matters: it blocks the CRYSPNet route. Retracted: 'the numeric-cell-to-symmetry mapping our RF performs is a published task'.

2411.00803.title: Designing a Dataset for Convolutional Neural Networks to Predict Space Groups Consistent with Extinction Laws
2411.00803.verdict: ROW B adjacent, overlap OVERSTATED in my first verdict. Its ceiling is ANALYTIC (extinction laws give the maximum in closed form for a synthetic pattern); ours is EMPIRICAL (a reconstruction on actual renders). Same goal, route unavailable to us.

2603.16253.title: Grounding the Score: Explicit Visual Premise Verification for Reliable Vision-Language Process Reward Models
2603.16253.verdict: ROW C ADJACENT, NOT OCCUPIED — publishes the perception/reasoning ENTANGLEMENT problem in verifiers (cite as motivation). Unoccupied: a DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRIC checker that cannot misperceive, since every cited verifier is itself learned.

2512.21329.title: Your Reasoning Benchmark May Not Test Reasoning: Revealing Perception Bottleneck in Abstract Reasoning Benchmarks
2512.21329.verdict: CLOSEST NEIGHBOUR, MISSED BY THE FIRST TWO PASSES. Challenges the reasoning-deficit interpretation of the ARC gap and hypothesises it arises primarily from limitations in VISUAL PERCEPTION, verified with a two-stage pipeline explicitly separating perception from reasoning. WE MUST STOP CLAIMING perception-as-bottleneck as a finding. OUR DELTA, and it is real: their perception stage converts each image to a natural-language description WITH A MODEL, so their separation is model-mediated and inherits the describer's errors. Ours is a DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRIC inversion with a closed-form ground truth, giving a numeric ceiling rather than a two-stage comparison.

2504.15280.title: Seeing from Another Perspective: Evaluating Multi-View Understanding in MLLMs
2504.15280.verdict: ADJACENT — All-Angles Bench, 2100+ annotated multi-view QA pairs over 90 real scenes, testing multi-view geometric consistency and cross-view correspondence. Establishes that multi-view correspondence is a known MLLM weakness, which SUPPORTS our premise. Not occupied: real scenes with human annotation, no closed-form ceiling, and no crystallography.

The unoccupied claim rests on fifteen searched works, not an exhaustive search.
